summary: npm package used as a CDN vehicle to serve a browser redirect script via jsDelivr
details: Package `main` is `px.js`, a browser-only script (references `document.*`) that injects a full-viewport iframe pointing at `https://mfmz.equnjx.cn/H.html?c=0gjr`. The tarball also ships `update_px8my.sh`, a maintainer workflow script that rotates the destination domain, bumps the version, runs `npm publish`, and then purges jsDelivr's cache for `/npm/px8my/px.js` — indicating the package is used as a CDN redirect distribution channel via jsDelivr, not as a Node library. There are no `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` lifecycle hooks, no top-level require-time side effects, and the `main` script is inert under Node (it only exercises `document.*`). A developer who runs `npm install px8my` or `require('px8my')` in a Node project is not harmed — the payload only affects end-users of web pages that load `px.js` from jsDelivr as a `<script>` tag. Registry abuse worth deplatforming, but not an installer-side supply-chain attack under this system's threat model.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
